statements.t: The Company’s operations over the last several years generally reflect three strategies which the Company expects to continue: (i) increased attention to “niche” insurance products, such as the Company’s funeral plan policies and traditional whole life products; (ii) increased emphasis on the funeral home and cemetery business; and (iii) capitalizing on the housing market by originating mortgage loans.
The Company expects to pay out liabilities under its funeral plans over the long term given the nature of those plans.

Because of the long-term nature of these liabilities, the Company can hold to maturity or for the targeted investment period its corresponding bond, real estate, and mortgage loan investments, thus reducing the risk of liquidating these long-term investments because of any sudden changes in their fair values.
The Company purchases short-term investments on a temporary basis to meet the expected short-term requirements of the Company’s insurance products.
